definitions.explanation: A high-status Shinto shrine, typically one with imperial connections or dedicated to the imperial family or a major deity. Higher in rank than a regular shrine ({神社|じんじゃ}). When used alone without a place name, it usually refers to Ise Jingu, the most sacred Shinto shrine.

examples.japanese: {伊勢神宮|いせじんぐう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{参拝|さんぱい}した→参拝する：15627_sanpaisuru⟧。
{明治神宮|めいじじんぐう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{東京|とうきょう}→東京：09564_toukyou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{最|もっと}も→最も：01736_mottomo⟧⟦{有名|ゆうめい}→有名：01106_yuumei⟧な{神宮|じんぐう}だ。
examples.english: Meiji Jingu is the most famous grand shrine in Tokyo.

examples.japanese: {神宮|じんぐう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{神社|じんじゃ}→神社：01620_jinja⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中|なか}→中：00654_naka⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{特|とく}に→特に：01260_tokuni⟧⟦{格式|かくしき}→格式：16025_kakushiki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{高|たか}い→高い：00500_takai⟧⟦{神社|じんじゃ}→神社：01620_jinja⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{指|さ}す→指す：02056_sasu⟧。
examples.english: Jingu refers to shrines of particularly high rank among Shinto shrines.

notes:
USAGE:
{神宮|じんぐう} is a title given to shrines of the highest status in Shinto. Not all shrines can use this title — it is reserved for those with connections to the imperial family or major deities.

KEY EXAMPLES:
- {伊勢神宮|いせじんぐう} (Ise Grand Shrine) — the holiest Shinto shrine, dedicated to Amaterasu
- {明治神宮|めいじじんぐう} (Meiji Shrine) — dedicated to Emperor Meiji
- {熱田神宮|あつたじんぐう} (Atsuta Shrine) — houses the sacred sword Kusanagi

SHRINE HIERARCHY:
{神宮|じんぐう} (grand shrine) > {大社|たいしゃ} (great shrine) > ⟦{神社|じんじゃ}→神社：01620_jinja⟧ (shrine). The exact hierarchy is complex and debated, but {神宮|じんぐう} generally indicates the highest prestige.
